A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same Skip-BART/RPMC-L2 study. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons, ablations and a 38-participant human evaluation, with additional results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds pre-training ablations and a 30-participant cross-genre evaluation, including Appendix E results.

M1.justification: The core architecture, losses and inference procedure are retained; expanded pre-training descriptions document existing components. However, v2 Equation 12 specifies rounded, (n+1)-weighted intensity labels, unlike v1 Equation 2. The PDFs do not establish whether this changes actual training-label construction or represents a documentation correction or error.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on three Suno-generated songs spanning folk, R&B and jazz, extending coverage beyond the recorded rock, punk, metal and core material. The original 699-sample RPMC-L2 dataset and DEAM baseline-training data remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds two evaluated comparator variants: pre-training with fixed rather than random MASK tokens, and pre-training without the discriminator. Existing ablations and the Hsiao-inspired rule-based comparator using DEAM-trained emotion recognition and Nijdam's color mapping are retained.

E3.justification: v2 adds a temporal-change metric, corr(|Δ|), and a separate 30-participant evaluation of three generated songs without a ground-truth lighting condition. The original 38-participant study, 10 Hz sampling, sequence-length limit and 8:1:1 dataset split remain, with several settings relocated to appendices.

E4.justification: New ablations separately test random masking and the adversarial discriminator, beyond v1's combined training-from-scratch comparison. The cross-genre study adds a substantive generalization test. Existing visualization analysis is mostly retained and relocated, although v1 Figure 5b's example is omitted.

E5.justification: The original mean/SD reporting, repeated-measures ANOVA, sphericity correction and Bonferroni-adjusted comparisons remain. Cross-domain tables extend existing descriptive and pairwise-significance reporting rather than introducing a new statistical procedure. Neither version reports training-seed uncertainty.

E6.justification: v2 adds temporal-correlation scores, two ablation rows and cross-domain results, including overall ratings of 4.34 for Skip-BART versus 3.34 for rule-based lighting, with p<0.001. Table 1 also changes rule-based Value RMSE from 93.84 to 93.39, from-scratch Value RMSE from 68.49 to 67.49, and Skip-BART Hue MAE from 28.71 to 28.72. These are reported-value revisions, not established rerun improvements. Original in-domain human-study results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The written light-label definitions change: v1 Equations 1–2 use generic histograms and an unrounded mean, whereas v2 Equations 11–12 specify integer-bin counts and a rounded mean with (n+1) weights. This is a limited formal revision with unclear implementation consequences. Main loss, sampling and Von Mises mixture mathematics remain.

C1.justification: v2's introduction adds an explicit claim of successful cross-domain performance on other music styles. The central claims of first generative end-to-end ASLC, the RPMC-L2 contribution, and performance approaching human lighting engineers are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about broader genre generalization, real-time music prediction and photosensitivity risks, plus an interpretation of sampling randomness as apparent creativity. It removes v1's explicit warning about bias from substituting components in the reproduced baseline, although the general quantitative-comparison fairness caveat remains.

D1.justification: New Appendix A specifies previously undisclosed masking ratios, pre-training loss weights, the three-layer LeakyReLU regressor and discriminator structure. Appendix C.3 specifies one-second audio windows with 0.1-second hops. These substantially expand documentation of existing procedures; the model-configuration and hardware settings remain. v2 also adds a supplementary-material availability statement.

R1.justification: v2 removes the Transformer-in-MIR background subsection and associated citations, including Video2Music and UniAudio, while adding MidiBERT-Piano and transfer-learning references. Its central novelty positioning against rule-based stage-lighting methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: processing, detailed experimental setup and visualization material move into appendices; contributions and limitations are rewritten; the Transformer-in-MIR subsection disappears; and ethics and reproducibility statements are added. RSTC terminology is standardized without establishing a new sampling procedure.

P2.justification: The layout changes from two columns to one. Table 1 gains comparator rows and metric columns, Tables 2–3 gain cross-domain sections, and Tables 8–9 are added. v2 Figure 5 combines v1 Figure 5a with the earlier main-text Figure 4, omitting the former Figure 5b; other figures are relocated and resized.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens support for the pre-training design through targeted ablations, adds limited evidence beyond the training genres, and fills important reproducibility gaps in Appendix A. These provide a modest net improvement. The generalization evidence covers only three generated songs, the baseline-bias qualification is weakened, and the revised intensity-label equation leaves an indexing ambiguity. The core method and original human-study findings remain largely unchanged.
